svg.aria-label: Comparison between Fixed Capital plus Current Account system vs Fluctuating Capital Account system for partnerships
svg.text: Fixed Capital System vs. Fluctuating Capital System
Most partnerships prefer the FIXED Capital System (2 separate accounts per partner) so permanent investment stays crystal clear!
Method 1: FIXED Capital System (2 Accounts — Preferred!)
Account A: Partner's Capital Account (STAYS FIXED!)
• Records ONLY original permanent capital introduced
(plus any permanent new capital or capital withdrawal)
✓ Makes calculating Interest on Capital super clean!
Account B: Partner's Current Account (Fluctuates Yearly)
Cr (+): Interest on Capital, Partner Salary, Share of Profit
Dr (−): Drawings, Interest on Drawings, Share of Loss
• Instantly exposes if a partner overdrew beyond profit
(a DEBIT Current Account balance = overdrawn partner!)
Method 2: FLUCTUATING Capital System (1 Combined A/c)
Single Combined Capital Account (Changes Every Year!)
CREDITED with (+):
• Opening Capital + New Capital Introduced
• Interest on Capital, Partner Salary & Share of Profit
DEBITED with (−):
• Drawings, Interest on Drawings & Share of Loss
Closing Balance changes up or down EVERY year!
Drawback: Original invested capital gets mixed up with
yearly profits & drawings — harder to track overdrawings!
When Partner Contributes Cash + Assets (e.g. Van): Dr Bank $X · Dr Motor Vehicles $Y / Cr Partner's Capital A/c $(X+Y)
